description: The group is geographically dispersed enough that every real candidate leaves someone over their stated comfortable travel tolerance. Leximin still picks a defensible answer — it minimizes the worst burden, it does not promise everyone comfort, and it does not defer to the better-rated venue.

candidateVenues.name: Herbert Samuel Grill
candidateVenues.note: On Keren and Doron's doorstep, and the better-rated venue — but 10.45 km from Amit against a tolerance of 8, a burden of 1.307.

candidateVenues.name: Kfar Bat Yam Midpoint Grill
candidateVenues.note: Roughly equidistant from all three: 5.77 km for Keren and Doron against a tolerance of 5, a burden of 1.154 each, and 6.23 km for Amit against 8, a burden of 0.778. Over tolerance for two of the three, and the lowest-rated option.

expected.reasoning: Every candidate leaves someone over tolerance, so there is no 'solution' in the strict sense — but leximin still forces a single answer here, and it is not the comfortable one. Straight-line burdens (distance / toleranceKm, computed from the coordinates in this file): Herbert Samuel is [1.307 Amit, 0.006 Doron, 0.006 Keren] and Kfar Bat Yam is [1.154 Keren, 1.154 Doron, 0.778 Amit]. Leximin compares the worst-off participant first: 1.154 beats 1.307, so Kfar Bat Yam wins outright and the second and third entries are never reached. It wins despite being the lower-rated venue and despite putting two of the three over tolerance rather than one, because leximin minimizes the worst burden and has no exchange rate between kilometres and stars (spec §5.4). That is the thing this scenario checks. Agreed by the team on this basis. Note the numbers above are straight-line distances with no detour factor: the two participants are 10.4 km apart as the crow flies and rather further by road, and it is the straight line the burden formula is defined on — the system does not compute driving or travel time (spec §5.4).
